message.content: Nicolaus Copernicus developed his heliocentric theory during the Renaissance, a period of profound intellectual awakening in Europe. The political landscape was fragmented, with the Holy Roman Empire and various kingdoms competing for power and influence. Religious authority dominated daily life, making any challenge to established cosmology both dangerous and revolutionary. His model bore a cactiform resemblance to ancient Greek ideas that had been suppressed for centuries. The Church's grip on thought made publication risky, so Copernicus delayed releasing his work until near his death.
